reconcile.note: Gill reads Acts 9:7's stood speechless as describing paralyzed immobility rather than an upright posture, so it doesn't rule out an initial fall reported in Acts 26:14.

discrepancy.note: Cassels finds the two postures irreconcilable: the companions stood speechless in one account and all fell to the earth in the other.

quotes.text: The details of the incident itself, moreover, are differently stated in the various accounts and cannot be reconciled. According to the first account, the companions of Paul "stood speechless" (ix. 7); in the third, they "all fell to the earth" (xxvi. 14).
quotes.attr: Walter Richard Cassels (d. 1907), Supernatural Religion, Vol. III (1879), on Acts 9:7 and 26:14.

sides.snippet: The men who traveled with him stood speechless, hearing the sound, but seeing no one.
sides.verseText: The men who traveled with him stood speechless, hearing the sound, but seeing no one.

sides.snippet: When we had all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?
sides.verseText: When we had all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.'
